radar.title: In Which Matching Markets Do Costly Compatibility Inspections Lead to a Deadlock?
radar.summary: A key feature of many real-world matching markets is congestion, i.e., market participants struggle to find match partners. We characterize congestion in a model of random matching markets where an agent pair must perform a mutual inspection to verify compatibility prior to matching with each other. Motivated by the notion of regret-free stability, we assume an agent pair is only willing to {perform a mutual inspection if they are each other's current favorite agent, which guarantees a match if the inspection finds compatibility.} We ask when, in large random two-sided markets, will \emph{information deadlocks} arise in which many agents delay inspections indefinitely awaiting a match guarantee. The market consists of $N$ women and $\alpha N$ men. We characterize the existence and size of information deadlock as a function of the men-to-women ratio $\alpha$, women’s average consideration-set size $K$, and an inspection's success probability $p$, as the number of women $N$ grows. We find a phase transition from a deadlock-free regime (where a vanishingly small fraction of agents are stuck waiting) to the information deadlock regime as $K$ increases, $\alpha$ decreases, or $p$ decreases. Several market-design insights emerge from our characterization. For example, the level of market connectivity $K$ that maximizes the number of matches formed is the level that places the market at the phase boundary between the deadlock-free regime and the deadlock regime. Vertical differentiation between agents reduces deadlock, as does a willingness by agents to {inspect with their top-$k$ current favorites for $k > 1$.} Our analysis is inspired by the machinery of message passing and density evolution from statistical physics, and the emergence of deadlock corresponds to a branching process of preferred partners becoming supercritical.

A Better Cycle-Breaker for Direct Democracy?
radar.summary: When a counter-proposal is made to an initiative to change the Swiss constitution, the citizenry makes three binary majority choices: the initiative versus the status quo, the initiative versus the counter-proposal, and the status quo versus the counterproposal as a tie-breaker. If there is a cycle, the alternative that beats the status-quo wins. This system invites strategic voting, as exemplified by the 2010 case of the “Ausschaffungsinitiative”. We suggest to break cycles differently by choosing the middle alternative in case of a cycle, which will normally be the counter-proposal. More precisely, we show that there always exists a strong Nash equilibrium in which all citizens vote sincerely. Moreover, the outcome of all alternative strong equilibria with strategic voting is the same as if everybody votes sincerely. We also show that other common cycle-breaker rules cannot achieve the same result.

radar.title: Sustainable Multi-Zone Greenhouse Fertigation Through Reliability-Aware Sensing, Spatiotemporal Graph Learning, and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
radar.summary: With protected agriculture increasingly developing toward large-scale, multi-zone, and intelligent production, reducing water and fertilizer consumption, drainage losses, and energy waste while maintaining crop yield, product quality, and long-term economic profitability has become an important challenge for sustainable greenhouse production. To address sensor abnormalities, spatial heterogeneity among irrigation zones, competition for shared hydraulic resources, and the limited ability of conventional control strategies to jointly optimize resource efficiency and economic performance, a sensor-driven spatiotemporal graph multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, termed SensorGraph-FertiMARL, is proposed for state sensing, response prediction, and sustainable coordinated fertigation optimization in multi-zone greenhouses. Reliable zone-level states are first obtained through sensor-reliability gating, missing-state reconstruction, and multi-relational graph fusion incorporating spatial, hydraulic, and microclimatic relationships. An action-conditioned fertigation–yield–quality–profit digital twin is then constructed to jointly predict root-zone responses, resource consumption, marketable yield, product quality, and net profit associated with candidate control actions. Finally, graph-based multi-agent proximal policy optimization (Graph-MAPPO) with capacity, safety, and fairness constraints is employed to coordinate fertigation allocation among multiple zones under shared pump, main-pipeline, and nutrient-solution resource constraints. Evaluated through rigorous offline digital-twin simulation and replay testing calibrated against complete multi-stage historical dataset records from an eight-zone commercial greenhouse, experimental results show that the proposed method reduced water and fertilizer use to 75.8% and 78.3% (achieving water and fertilizer saving rates of 24.2% and 21.7%), respectively, relative to the uniform timer-based control baseline, while decreasing the drainage rate to 7.2%. The Grade-A product rate increased to 84.6%, net profit reached 138.9% of the baseline level (a +38.9% net-profit improvement), return on investment (ROI) reached 1.94, and the stress-violation rate was limited to 2.9%. For state sensing and digital-twin prediction, the sensor-state reconstruction mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2) were 0.036 and 0.918, respectively; the water-content prediction MAE was 0.041, the electrical conductivity (EC) prediction root mean squared error (RMSE) was 0.119, and the drainage prediction mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was 8.7%. In addition, the R2 for marketable-yield prediction reached 0.912, the macro-averaged F1 (Macro-F1) score for quality-grade prediction reached 0.851, the R2 for net-profit prediction reached 0.904, the mean prediction interval width (MPIW) was 0.142, and the prediction interval coverage probability (PICP) reached 0.931. These results demonstrate that SensorGraph-FertiMARL can simultaneously achieve water and fertilizer conservation, drainage reduction, operational-risk control, and economic improvement while maintaining marketable production and quality, thereby providing an effective intelligent optimization approach for resource-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and economically viable greenhouse production.

radar.title: Distributed Marginal Return: A Communication-Efficient Algorithm for Multi-Agent Weapon Target Assignment
radar.summary: The Weapon-Target Assignment (WTA) problem in distributed multi-agent systems is challenged by limited situational awareness and communication constraints. Existing distributed methods, such as auction-consensus algorithms, typically assume task-value independence, a simplification that fails to capture the coupled effects of multi-weapon assignments. This paper introduces the Distributed Marginal Return (DMR) algorithm, a novel decentralized approach that generalizes auction-consensus frameworks. DMR enables agents to compute bids based on marginal return and uses a consensus protocol to resolve conflicts, allowing multiple non-conflicting proposals to be accepted in parallel for cooperative optimization with minimal communication. A key theoretical contribution is our proof that the marginal returns of non-conflicting bids are additive, a property that ensures global consistency and validates our parallel acceptance mechanism. Extensive simulations demonstrate that DMR significantly outperforms baseline algorithms in both solution quality and communication efficiency, offering a scalable and robust solution for real-world distributed command and control applications.

radar.title: First-Order Bilevel Optimization for Non-truthful Auction Design
radar.summary: Automated mechanism design has enabled the learning of complex auction mechanisms using neural networks. However, designing non-truthful auctions remains challenging because bidders' equilibrium strategies depend on the auction mechanism and thus evolve as the mechanism is optimized. In this work, we formulate auction design as a Stackelberg game with multiple strategic followers and develop a fully first-order algorithm for revenue optimization in non-truthful auctions. We establish non-asymptotic guarantees for hypergradient approximation and show that, under standard smoothness and strong-monotonicity assumptions, our method reaches an $O(ε)$-stationary point using $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-2})$ first-order oracle calls. Experiments on symmetric and asymmetric single-item auctions, as well as multi-item auctions, show that our method converges faster than second- and zeroth-order baselines and scales better as the number of bidders increases. Our method also discovers auctions that achieve revenue close to truthful baselines. These results provide a scalable framework for automated mechanism design beyond truthful auctions.
radar.summary_short: Automated mechanism design has enabled the learning of complex auction mechanisms using neural networks. However, designing non-truthful auctions remains challenging because bidders' equilibrium strategies depend on the auction mechanism and thus evolve as the mechanism is optimized.

radar.title: At What Cost? (In)efficiency in First-Price Procurement Auctions
radar.summary: We study the efficiency of Bayes-Nash equilibria in first-price procurement auctions. We measure efficiency by the Price of Anarchy (PoA): the ratio between the expected social cost in equilibrium and the minimum expected social cost resulting from a socially optimal allocation. We first show that the standard first-price procurement auction has no bounded PoA guarantee. We construct equilibria in which every bidder is indifferent between all bids in a common interval, so that bids can be arbitrarily large, and the PoA is unbounded. If costs lie in an interval $[\underline c,\bar c]$ but bids are not restricted, the PoA equals the trivial ratio $\bar c/\underline c$. We hence study ways to restore a finite guarantee, first by characterizing the PoA when bids lie in $[\underline c,\bar c]$, which leads to the tight bound $1 + \frac1{e^2}(\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}-1)$. Alternatively, we introduce the notion of a phantom bidder: the auctioneer accepts the lowest bid only if it does not exceed a phantom bid, drawn independently of the costs, and otherwise buys from an outside option at cost $\bar c$. We show that a simple fixed phantom bid, i.e., a deterministic cap, gives PoA $=\frac1e\sqrt {\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}}+O(1)$. We further show that no phantom mechanism whose construction depends only on the cost interval, under a mild regularity condition, whatever distribution it uses and whatever it reveals about the phantom bid before bidding, can improve on the $\sqrt{\frac{\bar c}{\underline c}}$ dependence.
radar.summary_short: We study the efficiency of Bayes-Nash equilibria in first-price procurement auctions. We measure efficiency by the Price of Anarchy (PoA): the ratio between the expected social cost in equilibrium and the minimum expected social cost resulting from a socially optimal allocation.

Online LLM Inference Routing for Multi-Agent Systems under Long-Term Budget and Layered Privacy Constraints
radar.summary: Abstract The Cloud-Edge-End (CEE) collaborative architecture has become a key paradigm for deploying highly intelligent multi-agent systems with low latency and high energy efficiency. Existing studies on efficient task offloading in CEE, however, either overlook long-term financial budget constraints from commercial API token usage and edge computing leasing, or inadequately handle layered information-sharing and privacy restrictions in decentralized autonomous agents. This paper investigates online inference routing to minimize the computational and communication overhead of large language model (LLM) workloads under long-term budget constraints, agent intent-sharing limitations, and un-known future prompt lengths. We propose a budget-aware online optimization framework that uses Lyapunov optimization to decouple long-term financial constraints, and show that the decoupled problem forms a generalized ordinal potential game. To address heterogeneous information-sharing restrictions, we design an adaptive best response algorithm for cooperative environments with shared decision information, and a multi-agent distributed routing algorithm for limited-information environments, enabling efficient offloading without inter-agent intent sharing. Theoretical analysis provides conditional performance and queue-length bounds and establishes finite convergence of the per-slot solvers. Simulations on distributed inference testbeds show that our scheme reduces the inference overhead of heterogeneous agentic tasks while achieving a favorable trade-off between performance and actual token expenditure.

radar.title: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
radar.summary: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. We propose an axiomatic framework that derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry and Linearity), treating them as structural constraints rather than heuristic design choices. This formulation builds on a novel NAHT decomposition, which characterises the fundamental difference between open and fully controllable multi-agent systems, and establishes a cooperative game-theoretic foundation for learning. We further show that enforcing these axioms on learning individual value functions recovers the Shapley value for Dec-POMDPs, providing a principled bridge between reinforcement learning and classical cooperative game theory. Building on this framework, we introduce Shapley Machines and Banzhaf Machines, two generic algorithmic templates that can be instantiated with standard reinforcement learning methods. When applied to strong base algorithms such as IPPO and POAM, our methods consistently improve learning efficiency and generalisation to unseen agent types and conventions across NAHT benchmark tasks. The code of experiments is published on https://github.com/hsvgbkhgbv/axiomatic-rl-naht.
radar.summary_short: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design.

radar.title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
radar.venue_raw: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
radar.summary: Multi-agent systems of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding across domains, introducing dynamics not captured by single-agent evaluations. Yet, existing work has mostly contrasted the behavior of a single agent with that of a collective of fixed size, leaving open a central question: How does group size shape dynamics? Here, we move beyond this dichotomy and systematically explore outcomes across the full range of group sizes. We focus on multi-agent misalignment, building on recent evidence that interacting LLMs playing a simple coordination game can generate collective biases absent in individual models. First, we show that collective bias is a deeper phenomenon than previously assessed: Interaction can amplify individual biases, introduce new ones, or override model-level preferences. Second, we demonstrate that group size affects the dynamics in a nonlinear way, revealing model-dependent dynamical regimes. Finally, we develop a mean-field analytical approach and show that, above a critical population size, simulations converge to deterministic predictions that expose the basins of attraction of competing equilibria. These findings establish group size as a key driver of multi-agent dynamics and highlight the need to consider population-level effects when deploying LLM-based systems at scale.

radar.title: Labtune: Treating Lab Organization and Information Sharing as Experimental Variables in LLM-Agent Discovery
radar.summary: De-siloing can create groupthink; silos can prevent knowledge sharing and reduce research efficiency. The same tension appears in research systems built with large language model (LLM) agents, yet their organization is usually fixed by design. I propose treating laboratory structure and information sharing as experimental variables. I introduce Labtune, an open framework for bounded research workflows with user-selected laboratory organization, communication policy, model configuration and budget. Users can choose among six editable designs, from multidisciplinary silos and transdisciplinary teams to co-leaders, hub-and-spoke structures, flat co-labs and a single scientist. Information sharing can independently vary from none to high detail, with an optional channel for conditional abstractions called wisdom. Sharing is enforced by the controller at phase barriers rather than through unrestricted agent chat, while delegation does not create additional budget or permissions. Development evidence is separated from protected confirmation, and an optional multi-lab layer allows laboratories with different structures to exchange filtered information. Labtune is an idea and system-description paper, not a benchmark result. Its contribution is to make laboratory organization and information sharing configurable and measurable under matched budgets. I do not claim that one design or level of sharing is best; the aim is to create a concrete experimental space in which those differences can be tested.

radar.title: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System for Bridge Operation and Maintenance based on Large Language Model
radar.summary: Bridges are critical transportation infrastructure, and reliable operation and maintenance (O&M) is essential for traffic safety and long-term structural performance. However, bridge O&M faces key bottlenecks: no unified architecture coordinates heterogeneous resources; model inferences lack clear links to physical-mechanical laws; and experts' tacit knowledge remains difficult to formalize. This study proposes a knowledge-enhanced autonomy formalization methodology and apply it to construct the Bridge O&M Multi-Modal Multi-Agent System (BOMMA), which integrates heterogeneous diagnostic actions, physics-mechanics-informed representations, long-term memory, and structured experiential knowledge within a coordinated multi-agent workflow, enabling interpretable and traceable scheduling, analysis, and decision-making. On 3,492 multi-source instructions, the proposed method achieves scheduling recalls of 85.37% for simple and 99.40% for composite tasks, with 95.35% BERT F1-score for O&M action reasoning. Ablation studies confirm the contributions of the components in the autonomy. This study bridges general LLM reasoning and specialized bridge O&M requirements.

radar.title: Verification Allocation in Stylized LLM Agent Pipelines under Hidden Tool Degradation: A Discrete-Time Mean-Field Analysis
radar.summary: We study a stylized verification-allocation model for role-structured pipelines with binary inherited corruption and hidden tool degradation. Standard contraction arguments give serial and multi-role fixed points and a finite-population deviation bound under independence. When verification actions affect neither future errors nor observations, the belief-state choice is myopic. We characterize a two-action threshold under an explicit monotonicity condition and a restricted four-action interval and tail policy when generation rates are equal and only one check degrades. Synthetic experiments check these model-specific results and find counterexamples outside the restriction. This is conditional model analysis, not a general mean-field-game result or empirical evidence about deployed LLM systems.

radar.title: Trading Off Business and Family Investments: Evidence from U.S. Entrepreneurial Households
radar.summary: Investing in children’s human capital reduces business investments for U.S. entrepreneurial households. Using financial account data of 90,000 small businesses linked to their owners and a regression discontinuity design that compares the business performance of households with college-aged dependents (18–22) to those with near-college-aged dependents (14–17), I show that business revenues and expenses decline sharply when owners’ children reach age 18. Despite the declines, profitability and productivity remain largely unaffected, suggesting a general downsizing rather than a loss in efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis shows that downsizing is concentrated among highly indebted owner households and businesses with volatile cash flows. For each dollar increase in household spending associated with a child turning 18, business expenses decline by $2.26. These findings are consistent with entrepreneurial parents reallocating capital from business investments toward their children’s human capital, as both compete for the same pool of internal family financial resources. radar.title: VIAS: Value-Isolating Activation Steering for Multi-Value Alignment and Compliance for Organisations
radar.summary: Organisations increasingly deploy large language model agents that must follow organisational values. We check whether activation steering, which adds vectors to a model's internal activations during generation without changing its weights, can improve compliance beyond prompting alone. Since most scenarios involve several values at once, we focus on multi-value steering. A simple way to build these vectors is to contrast responses that follow all values relevant to a scenario with responses that violate them. However, this gives nearly identical vectors for different values: they capture a general compliance signal rather than individual values, which limits their use when combining several values. We propose Value-Isolating Activation Steering (VIAS), which contrasts responses to the same scenario under two prompts, one listing all relevant values and one omitting a single target value. We keep a pair only if the target value changes from compliant to non-compliant and both responses still meet a minimum compliance level on the other values. We evaluate VIAS on PROTECT, a workplace compliance dataset where each scenario is tagged with relevant values from a 21-value taxonomy. VIAS reduces overlap between value vectors, making them better suited for multi-value steering, although this alone does not lead to independent control over each value. Combined with prompting, VIAS complies with every tagged value on 69.6% of scenarios for Qwen2.5-7B, 75.2% for Mistral-7B, and 72.6% for Phi-3.5-mini, outperforming prompting alone for all three models.

radar.title: INGENIERÍA ECONÓMICO-JURÍDICA, ACTUARIAL Y FINANCIERA DE SOCIEDADES POLICÉNTRICAS AUTÓNOMAS
radar.venue_raw: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
radar.summary: PROGRAMA/TESIS DOCTORAL INDEPENDIENTE Proyecto de investigación fundacional Arquitectura científica propuesta INGENIERÍA ECONÓMICO-JURÍDICA, ACTUARIAL Y FINANCIERA DE SOCIEDADES POLICÉNTRICAS AUTÓNOMAS Fundamentos para la transición hacia órdenes sociales privados, voluntarios, criptográficamente verificables, mutuales, cooperativos, industriales y patrimonialmente descentralizados. Subtítulo: Teoría de los polimonopolios endógenos multilocales, economías de capacidades, propiedad productiva, coordinación contractual y juegos evolutivos dinámicos endógenos volitivos. Objeto central: Construcción de un marco científico integral para estudiar las condiciones económicas, jurídicas, actuariales, financieras, tecnológicas e institucionales que permitirían la transición desde sociedades organizadas mediante monopolios territoriales de autoridad hacia sociedades de coordinación policéntrica, contractual, privada y voluntaria. Carácter de la investigación: Programa/Tesis doctoral independiente, interdisciplinar, teórico-analítica, matemático-institucional, propositiva y susceptible de contrastación empírica, no estrictamente austríaca, si tendientemente austríaca . Horizonte de investigación: 30 años. Ámbito de aplicación: Sistemas económicos locales, multilocales, industriales, digitales, transfronterizos y globales. Autoría: Fermín Ulaneo Fecha: Noviembre 2026. BLOQUE PRELIMINAR — PRESENTACIÓN Y FUNDAMENTOS DE LA INVESTIGACIÓN Este bloque comprende los elementos científicos, epistemológicos, metodológicos y conceptuales necesarios para establecer la identidad académica de la investigación. 1. Portada e identificación académica Título principal: Fundamentos para la transición hacia órdenes sociales privados Subtítulo científico: Teoría de los polimonopolios endógenos multilocales Naturaleza independiente de la investigación: Tesis doctoral independiente Autoría: Fermín Ulaneo. Fecha y lugar: Noviembre del 2026, España. Identificación institucional: No aplica. Clasificación científica: Interdisciplinar, teórico-analítica. Declaración de originalidad y trazabilidad documental: Susceptible de contrastación empírica. 2. Resumen ejecutivo de la investigación 2.1. Resumen general La investigación propone desarrollar una teoría integral de organización económica y jurídica basada en la coordinación voluntaria de individuos, empresas, propietarios, inventores, instituciones mutuales, organizaciones cooperativas y redes privadas de prestación de servicios. El objeto fundamental consiste en identificar, formalizar y evaluar las condiciones necesarias para constituir órdenes sociales capaces de coordinar producción, intercambio, financiación, protección patrimonial, resolución de conflictos, aseguramiento de riesgos, generación monetaria privada y provisión de infraestructuras sin depender estructuralmente de una autoridad territorial monopolística. La propuesta introduce una arquitectura institucional basada en siete elementos fundamentales: Policentrismo institucional: coexistencia de múltiples centros autónomos de decisión, contratación, financiación y prestación de servicios. Polimonopolios endógenos multilocales: organizaciones privadas que alcanzan posiciones de exclusividad económica mediante capacidades productivas, reputacionales, tecnológicas, contractuales y de coordinación, cuya continuidad depende de la aceptación voluntaria y de su capacidad para conservar clientes, capital y colaboradores. Mutualismo actuarial: agrupaciones voluntarias de personas y empresas para compartir riesgos mediante mecanismos de aseguramiento, reservas, reaseguro y distribución contractual de pérdidas. Propiedad productiva descentralizada: estructuras de propiedad, inversión, sucesión y capitalización capaces de multiplicar unidades productivas independientes. Infraestructuras monetarias y financieras privadas: sistemas de intercambio, liquidación, crédito, ahorro y financiación basados en reglas verificables y mecanismos competitivos. Resolución policéntrica de conflictos: instituciones especializadas en arbitraje, mediación, adjudicación y ejecución contractual. Juegos evolutivos dinámicos endógenos volitivos: una nueva arquitectura de análisis de decisiones estratégicas en la que los agentes pueden modificar preferencias, capacidades, compromisos, alianzas, reglas y estructuras de cooperación a lo largo del tiempo. La tesis no presupone que toda interacción económica sea necesariamente beneficiosa para todos los participantes. Investiga, por el contrario, bajo qué condiciones pueden transformarse conflictos distributivos, externalidades, incertidumbres y problemas de coordinación en procesos de creación conjunta de valor. El resultado esperado es una teoría institucional susceptible de formalización matemática, evaluación actuarial, análisis financiero, contrastación histórica y experimentación mediante simulaciones computacionales. 2.2. Abstract The research develops an interdisciplinary framework for the economic, legal, actuarial and financial foundations of polycentric voluntary societies. Its central objective is to investigate the institutional, technological and contractual conditions under which decentralized private organizations can provide economic coordination, insurance, monetary services, capital allocation, dispute resolution and productive infrastructure without relying on territorially monopolistic political authority. The proposed framework introduces endogenous multilocal poly-monopolies, voluntary mutual insurance architectures, decentralized productive ownership, private financial infrastructures, contractual governance and endogenous volitional evolutionary game theory. The research combines institutional economics, contract theory, mechanism design, actuarial mathematics, financial economics, cryptographic verification, evolutionary dynamics and industrial organization. Its principal scientific contribution is intended to be a formal and empirically testable architecture explaining how voluntary institutions emerge, compete, cooperate, adapt and reproduce across multiple geographical and technological environments. 2.3. Problema científico central ¿Cómo diseñar, financiar, asegurar, gobernar y reproducir sistemas sociales complejos en los que las funciones actualmente concentradas en instituciones territoriales monopolísticas puedan ser desarrolladas por redes autónomas, privadas, mutuales, cooperativas y contractuales? 2.4. Solución científica propuesta Desarrollar una arquitectura institucional multicapa que permita: Sustitución funcional progresiva de estructuras monopolísticas. Creación de organizaciones privadas de gobernanza. Desarrollo de sistemas monetarios competitivos. Provisión privada de servicios de protección, seguridad y justicia. Financiación industrial y tecnológica descentralizada. Aseguramiento mutual de riesgos sistémicos. Protección de derechos patrimoniales. Coordinación contractual entre jurisdicciones voluntarias. Expansión de las capacidades productivas humanas. Reducción de los costes de conflicto y cooperación. 2.5. Resultados y aportaciones esperadas La investigación aspira a producir: Una teoría económica de los polimonopolios endógenos. Una teoría actuarial de las sociedades mutuales autónomas. Una arquitectura jurídica de órdenes contractuales policéntricos. Un modelo financiero de capitalización institucional privada. Una teoría de transición monetaria sin banca central. Una teoría de transición institucional sin Estado. Una teoría evolutiva de cooperación y creación conjunta de valor. Un modelo cuantitativo de sostenibilidad intergeneracional. 3. Introducción general 3.1. Planteamiento del problema Las sociedades industriales contemporáneas concentran importantes funciones de coordinación económica, jurídica, monetaria, financiera y territorial en instituciones dotadas de facultades exclusivas. La investigación parte de una pregunta diferente: ¿Es posible desarrollar arquitecturas institucionales alternativas capaces de proporcionar esas mismas funciones, o funciones superiores, mediante organizaciones autónomas que compitan, cooperen, se especialicen y se coordinen voluntariamente? Esta pregunta requiere superar el tratamiento exclusivamente ideológico de la organización social. No basta con proponer la desaparición de una institución. Es necesario determinar: Qué funciones desempeña. Qué problemas resuelve. Qué incentivos sostienen su funcionamiento. Qué costes genera. Qué instituciones alternativas podrían asumir sus funciones. Qué mecanismos impedirían su captura. Cómo se financiarían. Cómo se asegurarían sus obligaciones. Cómo se resolverían los conflictos entre ellas. Cómo se produciría la transición sin provocar discontinuidades sistémicas. Por tanto, la abolición institucional, cuando sea objeto de la investigación, deberá estudiarse como un problema de sustitución funcional, no como una simple eliminación administrativa. 3.2. La unidad fundamental de análisis Se propone sustituir el análisis centrado exclusivamente en Estados, mercados nacionales y empresas individuales por una unidad institucional más amplia: La red autónoma de coordinación económico-jurídica. Esta unidad puede integrar: Individuos. Familias. Empresas. Cooperativas. Mutualidades. Aseguradoras. Organizaciones arbitrales. Redes de seguridad. Fondos de inversión. Instituciones monetarias. Plataformas tecnológicas. Organizaciones industriales. Redes de propietarios. Sistemas privados de acreditación y certificación. Cada organización constituye un agente institucional con recursos, capacidades, compromisos, derechos, obligaciones y mecanismos propios de adaptación. 3.3. Justificación de la investigación La investigación se justifica por la necesidad de integrar disciplinas que habitualmente estudian separadamente los problemas de organización social. Disciplina

radar.title: ATC: Agent Trajectory Control for Role-Contract Enforcement in Black-Box Multi-Agent Systems
radar.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems assign different responsibilities to different agents: one plans, another retrieves evidence, another verifies, another executes. This division of labor is only meaningful if each agent stays within the functions it is authorized to perform. Over many turns, however, an agent can produce a locally reasonable message that exercises authority belonging to another role: a verifier that begins planning, a retriever that asserts unsupported conclusions, an executor that changes state no one approved. We formalize this as role drift, a turn-level breach of an agent's role contract. We introduce Agent Trajectory Control (ATC), which makes each role's authority explicit as a contract and enforces it at the point where a message would enter the shared conversation. ATC scores a proposed output for out-of-role deviation, leakage into the functions of other roles, impermissible speech acts, and logical contract breaches, then computes a leakage-regularized target that constrains regeneration; the revised message is re-checked before admission. Enforcement acts on the message rather than the generator, so ATC governs agents whose internal representations are unavailable. Across homogeneous and heterogeneous teams, ATC improves task performance and role consistency while lowering role-drift energy relative to strong baselines spanning prompting, memory, workflow control, and activation editing, with the largest gains under explicit role-confusion stress tests and in larger, more diverse teams.
